introduction_markdown:
**Time allowed: three hours.** This paper contains six questions arranged in three sections: Section A - Physical and General Chemistry (questions 1 and 2); Section B - Inorganic Chemistry (questions 3 and 4); Section C - Organic Chemistry (questions 5 and 6).

Answer ALL the SIX questions in this booklet. The mark allocation is indicated for each question. Each question carries 20 marks. In calculations you are advised to show all the steps in your working, giving your answer at each stage. All necessary working must be shown. No marks will be awarded for answers without brief statements showing how the answers have been obtained. Noiseless calculators may be used.

**Useful data:** $R = 8.314\ \mathrm{J\,K^{-1}\,mol^{-1}}$ or $0.082\ \mathrm{atm\,dm^3\,K^{-1}\,mol^{-1}}$; one atmosphere (1 atm) = 1 Pa = $1.01\times10^{5}\ \mathrm{N\,m^{-2}}$ (as printed); relative atomic masses (RAM): C = 12.0, O = 16.0, S = 32.0, H = 1.0, Cl = 35.5.
incertitudes: Q4(b)(i)-(ii) : le sujet demande un composé où le soufre est au degré d'oxydation +7, qui n'existe pas réellement (le maximum est +6). Le corrigé retient l'ion peroxodisulfate S2O8(2-), dont le degré apparent est +7 si tous les oxygènes valent -2, et précise que le degré réel est +6 à cause du pont peroxyde.

Q4(c)(i) : SiO n'existe que comme espèce instable à haute température ; le corrigé l'indique. Les oxydes amphotères possibles sont plusieurs (PbO, SnO, SnO2, PbO2, GeO) : un seul est donné comme exemple.
Q4 : points imprimés 8 + 5 + 7 = 20, cohérents avec « Total = 20 marks ».

questions.enonce_markdown:
This question is on transition metal chemistry.

(i) Differentiate between a d-block element and a transition metal.

(ii) $[\mathrm{CrCl_2(H_2O)_4}]^+$ is a complex ion formed by a transition metal.

A: Name the complex and state the coordination number of the central metal ion.

Name: ......  Coordination number: ......

B: Give one condition which favours the formation of the complex.

(iii) The compound $\mathrm{Co(NH_3)_5BrSO_4}$ exhibits isomerism. State the type of isomerism exhibited by the compound and give the structures of the isomers.

Type of isomerism: ......  Structure of isomers: ...... *[8 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i)** A **d-block element** is any element whose atoms are filling the $d$ sub-shell (the elements of the block of the periodic table between group II and group III; e.g. Sc to Zn in the first row). A **transition metal** is a d-block element that **forms at least one stable ion with a partially filled d sub-shell** ($d^1$ to $d^9$). Scandium ($\mathrm{Sc^{3+}}$, $3d^0$) and zinc ($\mathrm{Zn^{2+}}$, $3d^{10}$) are d-block elements but are **not** transition metals.

**(ii) A:** the ion $[\mathrm{CrCl_2(H_2O)_4}]^+$ is the **tetraaquadichlorochromium(III) ion** (ligands in alphabetical order: aqua before chloro). Oxidation state of chromium: $x + 2(-1) + 4(0) = +1$, so $x = +3$. The **coordination number is 6** (four $\mathrm{H_2O}$ plus two $\mathrm{Cl^-}$ ligands, each donating one lone pair).

**B:** any one of: the central metal ion has **vacant low-energy d orbitals** to accept lone pairs from the ligands (small ion, high charge density); the ligands have **lone pairs of electrons** to donate; a **high concentration of the ligand** (excess ligand) drives the substitution in favour of the complex.

**(iii)** The type of isomerism is **ionisation isomerism**: the two isomers have the same formula but give different ions in solution, because the bromide and sulphate ions are exchanged between the coordination sphere (inside the brackets) and the free ions outside.

- $[\mathrm{Co(NH_3)_5Br}]\mathrm{SO_4}$: pentaamminebromocobalt(III) sulphate, gives free $\mathrm{SO_4^{2-}}$ (white precipitate with $\mathrm{BaCl_2}$ solution).
- $[\mathrm{Co(NH_3)_5SO_4}]\mathrm{Br}$: pentaamminesulphatocobalt(III) bromide, gives free $\mathrm{Br^-}$ (cream precipitate with $\mathrm{AgNO_3}$ solution).

questions.enonce_markdown:
This question concerns the chemistry of nitrogen and sulphur.

(i) Complete the table below by giving the formula and name of a compound in which sulphur exhibit the oxidation states -2 and +7.

| Oxidation state | Formula of compound | Name |
|---|---|---|
| -2 | | |
| +7 | | |

(ii) How does the +7 oxidation state in sulphur come about?

(iii) Give the main chemical equation, indicating the conditions for the manufacture of ammonia by the Haber process.

(iv) Give one industrial use of Nitric acid. *[5 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i)**

| Oxidation state | Formula of compound | Name |
|---|---|---|
| $-2$ | $\mathrm{H_2S}$ (or $\mathrm{Na_2S}$, $\mathrm{FeS}$) | hydrogen sulphide (or sodium sulphide, iron(II) sulphide) |
| $+7$ | $\mathrm{Na_2S_2O_8}$ (or $\mathrm{K_2S_2O_8}$), containing the $\mathrm{S_2O_8^{2-}}$ ion | sodium (or potassium) peroxodisulphate |

**(ii)** In the peroxodisulphate ion, $\mathrm{S_2O_8^{2-}}$, if **every oxygen atom is given the usual oxidation number $-2$**, then $2x + 8(-2) = -2$, so $x = +7$: this is how the apparent $+7$ oxidation state of sulphur comes about. In fact the ion contains a **peroxide link, $-\mathrm{O{-}O}-$**, in which the two oxygen atoms have oxidation number $-1$; taking this into account, $2x + 6(-2) + 2(-1) = -2$ gives $x = +6$, the true oxidation state (sulphur has only six valence electrons, so $+6$ is its maximum).

**(iii)** $\mathrm{N_2(g)} + 3\mathrm{H_2(g)} \rightleftharpoons 2\mathrm{NH_3(g)}$, $\Delta H = -92\ \mathrm{kJ\,mol^{-1}}$ (exothermic).

Conditions: a **temperature of about 450 $^\circ$C** (400 to 500 $^\circ$C, a compromise between rate and equilibrium yield), a **pressure of about 200 atm** (150 to 250 atm), and a **finely divided iron catalyst** (with promoters such as $\mathrm{K_2O}$ and $\mathrm{Al_2O_3}$). Unreacted nitrogen and hydrogen are recycled.

**(iv)** Nitric acid is used in the manufacture of **fertilisers** (ammonium nitrate); also of explosives (TNT, nitroglycerine), dyes and nitrate salts. (Any one use.)

questions.enonce_markdown:
The group IV elements are C, Si, Ge, Sn and Pb.

(i) Complete the table below by giving the formula of the oxides of the elements in the +2 and +4 oxidation states.

| Element | C | Si | Ge | Sn | Pb |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| +4 oxidation state | | | | | |
| +2 oxidation state | | | | | |

(ii) Give the formula of one oxide each which is

A: Neutral

B: Amphoteric

C: A greenhouse gas

(iii) Which of these elements exhibit allotropy? Give the allotropes of one of the elements. *[7 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i)**

| Element | C | Si | Ge | Sn | Pb |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| +4 oxidation state | $\mathrm{CO_2}$ | $\mathrm{SiO_2}$ | $\mathrm{GeO_2}$ | $\mathrm{SnO_2}$ | $\mathrm{PbO_2}$ |
| +2 oxidation state | $\mathrm{CO}$ | $\mathrm{SiO}$ (exists only as an unstable species at high temperature) | $\mathrm{GeO}$ | $\mathrm{SnO}$ | $\mathrm{PbO}$ |

Trend: the $+2$ state becomes more stable and the $+4$ state less stable down the group (inert pair effect), so lead(IV) oxide is a strong oxidising agent while tin(II) oxide is a reducing agent.

**(ii)**

- **A: Neutral:** $\mathrm{CO}$ (carbon monoxide; it does not react with water, acids or bases).
- **B: Amphoteric:** $\mathrm{PbO}$ (or $\mathrm{SnO}$, $\mathrm{SnO_2}$, $\mathrm{PbO_2}$, $\mathrm{GeO}$); for example $\mathrm{PbO} + 2\mathrm{HNO_3} \rightarrow \mathrm{Pb(NO_3)_2} + \mathrm{H_2O}$ and $\mathrm{PbO} + 2\mathrm{NaOH} + \mathrm{H_2O} \rightarrow \mathrm{Na_2[Pb(OH)_4]}$.
- **C: Greenhouse gas:** $\mathrm{CO_2}$ (carbon dioxide).

**(iii)** **Carbon** and **tin** exhibit allotropy (silicon and germanium are also found in crystalline and amorphous forms).

- Allotropes of **carbon**: **diamond** (each C bonded tetrahedrally to four others, a giant covalent lattice, very hard, an electrical insulator), **graphite** (layers of hexagonally arranged carbon atoms, each C bonded to three others, with delocalised electrons between the layers: soft, conducts electricity) and the **fullerenes** (e.g. $\mathrm{C_{60}}$, buckminsterfullerene).
- Allotropes of **tin**: grey tin ($\alpha$-tin, non-metallic, diamond structure, stable below 13 $^\circ$C) and white tin ($\beta$-tin, metallic, stable above 13 $^\circ$C).
